resources.string: One clipboard for this phone and your computers.
It made its own secret key, which never leaves it and lets your devices recognise this phone. Now connect a device: tap Connect a new device and scan the QR code it shows.
On a computer, run cbb pair and scan the code it shows.
I already use CBB on another phone
On a phone of the group, tap + and scan this code. On a computer of the group, tap + and type the numbers. Keep this screen open.
QR code to join the group
This TV joins the group of your phone: it shows a QR code, and the phone scans it.
My group was made on a computer
On the computer that created the group, run cbb pair -admin, then type the six-digit code it shows. Keep this phone on the same network.
On your phone, open CBB, tap + and scan this code. Keep this screen open.
Nothing new to send or fetch.

It can then add and remove devices with cbb pair and cbb remove. Its keys sit in a file on the computer: whoever copies that file can act as an admin until another admin removes it. Do this only for a computer you keep safe.
It can then add and remove devices with cbb pair and cbb remove. Its keys are in its hardware, which never lets them out.
It is an admin now: it adds and removes devices with cbb pair and cbb remove.
Another admin froze this computer, as one does with a stolen one: it changes nothing and the others refuse it. Unfreeze it only if it is in safe hands; otherwise remove it.
It will no longer sync with your devices. To add it again, scan its QR code again.
It made the group. This phone takes the group over with a new key, and the other devices follow it.
Removed. The other devices refuse it from now on.
Only an admin phone can add or remove devices.
Lost a phone? Make a second phone an admin: on it, tap I already use CBB on another phone, then scan its code here with +.
Point the camera at the QR code of cbb pair, or at the one your other phone shows.
Paste the text of the QR code of cbb pair.
The camera is not allowed. Allow it in the app\'s settings to scan, or paste the text of the QR code of cbb pair.
The camera did not start. Paste the text of the QR code of cbb pair instead.
The device is not ready yet. Trying again (%1$d)…
Join the group as an admin
Add a computer to your group
Remove a device from your group
Take the group over from the lost phone
Take the group the computer handed to this phone
Record where a device keeps its key
Renew the group\'s keys for sync away from home
Restore your group with the recovery key
The computer joined but did not confirm it. Check cbb status on it.
Connect this phone to your home Wi-Fi, then try again.
No phone scanned the code in five minutes. Try again.
Too many wrong codes. Try again with a new code.
Could not read the clipboard, so it was left as it is. Copy the text again, then try again.
This image is larger than 100 MB, so it stays on the computer.
This copy was not sealed to this phone, so it cannot be read here. Copy it again on that device.
This phone does not have the group\'s device list yet, so it cannot seal or read copies. Try again once a computer is connected.
Could not get the image from the computers. Copy it there again, then try again.
Only an admin phone can do this.
This computer keeps its keys in a file. Make it an admin first on its page, which warns what that means.
This computer is installed without root, so any of its programs can read its keys. It can never be an admin.
Could not reach the computer. Is it on the same network as this phone, and does its firewall let CBB in?
The code did not match. Run cbb pair on the computer again and scan the new code.
The computer refused. Run cbb pair on it again.
The other phone\'s group could not be joined. Try again.
No computer is waiting for a phone. Run cbb pair -admin on the computer that created the group, then try again.
Two computers are waiting for a device at once. Close cbb pair on one of them, then try again.
This computer did not open its window for a phone. Run cbb pair -admin on the computer that created the group.
The code did not match. Check the code on the computer\'s screen and type it again.
The computer\'s group could not be joined. Run cbb pair -admin on it again.
Set a screen lock on this phone first: the group\'s keys need it.
The fingerprint, face or screen lock was not confirmed, so nothing changed.
Add a fingerprint or face on this phone first: on Android 10 the group\'s keys need one.
This phone\'s group key was made by an earlier version of the app. Leave the group on this phone and set it up again.
%1$s needs %2$s installed first: take %2$s from the releases page.
The update failed; the app stays as it is.
Once a day the app checks for a release the project signed and installs it. The check tells GitHub this device\'s address, as any download does.
What they copy comes to this phone. Send sends what this phone copied.
Send this text to your computers?
%1$s handed CBB a text of %2$d characters. It goes to every computer of the group.
Saved in Downloads, in the folder CBB.
Sent to the computers, which fetch it from this phone now.
%1$s handed CBB %2$d items. They go to every computer of the group.
Sync the clipboard with your computers?
%1$s opened CBB. Syncing may put your computers\' latest copy on this phone\'s clipboard, where that app could read it.
Share, the selection menu and the cbb send entry let any app hand CBB a text or start a sync, so the phone asks first. "Always for this app" lets that one app go without asking.
None: the phone asks every app.

Notices when you copy text, then reads the clipboard for a moment and sends the text to your computers. With remote paste on, it puts an admin\'s text into the text field that has the focus. It reads nothing else on the screen.

Android lets an app read the clipboard only while it is in front. Turn CBB on in Accessibility, and what you copy goes to your computers without a tap; Android then says \"CBB pasted from your clipboard\" each time. Without it, use the Send clipboard tile, the notification\'s Send button, or Share.
If Android says the setting is restricted: open App info, tap ⋮, choose Allow restricted settings, then try again.
This phone is the group\'s hub

While the app is open, this phone is the hub of a group without a computer: the other phones, TVs and lite members on the home network connect to it, and with a forwarder they reach it from afar too. The forwarder only passes encrypted packets; it learns the group\'s tag, this phone\'s tunnel key and the addresses, never what is copied. A computer that is always on is the better hub; until then this phone does it.
Off: this phone is no hub.
Waiting for the app: the hub works while the app is open.
The hub at home only: add a forwarder for sync away from home.
Registered with the forwarder: devices away from home reach this phone.

The list of the project\'s entry points is out of date, and the forwarder does not answer on the ways this phone knows. Update CBB on a computer of the group, or import a new list there with cbb global entries import; the group passes it on when this phone meets it.
The forwarder does not take this phone. Check its address and key.
On a home network: devices here connect to this phone.
This network is not one of the hub\'s home networks: devices here do not see this phone.
This phone is on no Wi-Fi or Ethernet network now, so there is none to call home.
Reached from afar through the project\'s forwarder at cbb.tools. To use your own, enter its address and key.
To go back to the project\'s forwarder, empty both fields and save.
Give the forwarder\'s address with its port and its key, as cbb forward prints them, or leave both empty.
Keep the hub running in the background (uses the battery)
This phone is the hub: sync works while the app is open.
This phone is the hub, in the background too.

When the phone is not on the home network, it syncs through the WireGuard tunnel of your own hub, a computer of the group set up with cbb global hub; its port is reachable from the internet, but only through WireGuard with the group\'s keys. The hub answers this phone the next time it connects at home. Nothing goes anywhere else, and without the tunnel there is no connection. Turning it off forgets this phone\'s tunnel key.
Waiting for the hub: open the app at home once, near a computer of the group.
Connecting to the hub through the tunnel…
Connected to the hub through the tunnel.
Connected to the hub %1$s through the tunnel.
For networks that block WireGuard. VLESS needs a forwarder that takes it.
Change how the hub\'s tunnel hides?
Your devices get the new settings the next time they meet this hub at home; until then they do not reach it away from home.
The group\'s hub, in use now
The hub does not answer through the tunnel.
Error messages show the error underneath them, to find out what failed. Tap the version seven times to see this switch.
Every device of the group shows the new name.
Renamed. The other devices show the new name as soon as they hear of it.
One tap sends what this phone copied to your computers.
Its copies stay on it and the group\'s do not come; sending or fetching by hand still works.
Its copies go to the group, and the group\'s come to it.
The group\'s copies come to it; its own stay on it.
Its copies go to the group; the group\'s do not come.
The computer did not answer. It may be offline, or run an older version of CBB.
The app notifies of these as soon as it hears of them; the service hears of them in the background too. A paired watch shows them as well.
A device joined or was removed
A device was frozen or unfrozen
The hub does not answer away from home
%1$s was frozen: the others refuse it until an admin unfreezes it.
%1$s took the group over: it holds the group\'s root now.
For a device that is not on your network, such as a parent\'s computer: share the invitation file with its owner, who joins with cbb pair -invite. It works once, for an hour, while this app is open.
The invitation is open until %1$s. Share its file only with the person who joins: anyone who has it can ask to join.
A device (%1$s) used the invitation. Admit it only if the device shows the same fingerprint:
The device joined the group; it appears in the list once it connects.
The invitation expired without being used.
The invitation closed after three failed attempts. Make a new one.
An invitation needs the hub registered with its forwarder. Check the forwarder above.
Move the hub to a computer
Move the hub to a computer
A computer that is always on keeps sync away from home working while this app is closed. The devices that reach this phone from afar move with it.
Save a forwarder above first: away from home, the devices reach the new hub through it.
%1$s is always on. Make it the hub, so that sync away from home works while this app is closed?
The devices that reach this phone from afar move to %1$s, and this phone becomes its client. Sync away from home must be on there (cbb global on).
The computer is the hub now; this phone reaches it from afar.
The computer did not become the hub.
Your devices then reach the group through it when they are away from home, through the project\'s forwarder at cbb.tools. Sync away from home must be on there already; only its own user turns it on.
It is a hub now: your devices reach the group through it when they are away from home.
The computer did not become a hub.
A hub that reads the copies
A hub that only passes them on
A hub that reads the copies is an admin. A hub that only passes them on cannot read them: they are sealed to your other devices only, so its keys need no hardware.
It is a hub now that only passes the copies on: your devices reach the group through it when they are away from home, and it reads none of them.
The hub can move only while it runs with a forwarder.
Off: this phone meets nobody at a relay.
Waiting: the relay works while the app syncs.
At the relay: no other device of the group is there now.
At the relay; devices of the group there: %1$d.
The relay does not take this phone. Check its address and key.
Give the relay\'s address with its port and its key, as cbb relay prints them, or leave both empty.

For a group without a hub of its own: the devices meet at a relay, such as one set up with cbb relay, while the app syncs. The clipboard stays encrypted between the devices, but the relay learns which of them are online and their addresses, and which talk to each other, when and how much. Leave both fields empty to stop.

The clipboard stays encrypted end to end between the devices: the relay cannot read it or pose as a device. It does learn, while the devices use it, which devices of the group are online and their internet addresses, and which of them talk to each other, when and how much they send. A hub of the group\'s own lets none of this out. Use a relay you run yourself, or one whose operator you trust with this.
It goes where %1$s\'s keyboard focus is, once its user turned remote paste on there.
Left empty, the phone\'s clipboard goes.

A paste suits most apps; typing suits those that take no paste, and only up to 4 KB. Enter runs a command in a terminal, so the computer takes it only when its user allowed that. A secret leaves no trace in the computer\'s log or clipboard.
%1$s has no quick action turned on. Its user turns them on there, with sudo cbb action enable.
The computer defines what each action does, and runs it only for the admins its user allowed.
It happens a minute from now; until then, Cancel the reboot or shutdown stops it.
The device did not run the action.
Turn off the quick actions on %1$s?
No admin can run them there until its user turns them on again on the device itself.
The quick actions are off there.
Let the group\'s admins paste here

An admin of the group then puts a text into the text field that has the focus on this phone, from its own app or with cbb paste. This phone shows who pasted, and keeps a log of the last pastes without their text. Never on the lock screen.
It pastes through the service "Send my copies by themselves", which is off: turn it on in the system\'s accessibility settings.
It pastes through CBB\'s accessibility service, which is off: turn it on in the TV\'s settings, under Accessibility.
The accessibility service is on in the settings, but the system stopped it. Turn it off and on again there.
This phone types into a TV, a tablet, a console or a computer it is paired with, which needs nothing installed: the clipboard, at your tap, or a remote paste from an admin of the group.
This phone cannot act as a keyboard: its maker left the Bluetooth keyboard profile out of the system.
CBB may not use Bluetooth yet.
The system did not let this phone be a keyboard. Another app may be the phone\'s keyboard now: turn it off there.
Pick the device to type into.
Connecting… The device must be on and near.
No paired devices yet. Make this phone visible, then add it on the device, in its Bluetooth settings.
A paste from an admin then goes to that device instead of this phone. Remote paste must be on above; a text with a line break needs Enter allowed.
The device\'s layout has no key for: %1$s. Pick its layout above.
The watch is an admin now. It can freeze an admin computer, remove a device that is no admin and turn things off.
The watch did not answer. Is it connected to this phone, with CBB installed?
The watch needs a screen lock. Set one on the watch, keep it on your wrist, then try again.

With a key of its own, the watch can freeze an admin computer, remove a device that is no admin, and turn remote paste, quick actions and sync away from home off. It needs a screen lock, and its on-wrist detection should be on.
To give a new watch the key, remove this one from the devices first.
Drag to arrange. Drop a device on a collection to put it in.
Drag devices here, or add them with Move to collection in a device\'s menu.
The tiles stay as they were: that change does not fit.
Resolve a conflict in your group
The claim is cancelled. The other devices hear of it as soon as they connect.
Both histories are void. The device signs its records again by itself.
The group is stopped: its devices exchange only their records, no clipboard, until the group\'s root decides.
The group sends no secrets until its root decides.
%1$s signed two histories with one key, as a stolen key or a restore from a backup would.
Admins removed or froze each other without seeing it: %1$s. The root removes one of them.
Two claims to take the group over: %1$s.
%1$s claims the group, to take it over from its root.
%1$s claims the group, to take it over from its root: it takes effect in %2$s.
%1$s claims the group, and the group is stopped until its root decides.
The group holds %1$d records of a later version: update the app to read them.
The group is yours to take
The computer that held the group handed it to this phone. Take it to make this phone the group\'s root; the computer stays in the group.
This phone is the group\'s root now. The other devices hear of it as soon as they connect.
I have the group\'s recovery sheet

Point the camera at the QR code on the recovery sheet. Keep this phone on the network of a computer of the group. This phone becomes the group\'s root when the group\'s waiting time ends, unless the old phone cancels it.
The claim is sent. This phone becomes the group\'s root when the waiting time ends; Home shows the time left.
This is not the QR code of a recovery sheet.
This phone is in a group already. A recovery sheet restores a group on a phone without one.
Scan the QR code of the recovery sheet: on a new phone the typed key is not enough. A computer of the group takes the typed key with cbb recovery.
The computers found on this network are of another group than the sheet.
This is not the group\'s recovery key now: the root phone removed it or made a new one.
The computer\'s answer does not fit the group\'s records.
No computer of the group was found on this network. Turn one on and keep this phone on its network, then try again.
Change which keys may be admins
Change how long a copy from another device lasts

How long a copy from another device waits to go into this device\'s clipboard, counted from when it was copied. After that it is gone, and the button sends what this device copied. The whole group follows it.
Saved. Every device of the group follows it.
Which devices may be the group\'s admins and hubs. Keys in hardware never leave the device; whoever gets a key in a file can copy it. Admins already in the group stay until you remove them.
Saved. Every device of the group follows it.
This phone\'s own key is not proven, so the group cannot ask for proven keys yet.
The group\'s admin keys setting does not let this device\'s keys be an admin. Change it in Settings, Admin keys.
An admin reads the copies, so it is a hub that reads them too, not one that only passes them on.
The group then lets keys in files be admins and hubs (Settings, Admin keys).
A sheet to print and keep away from your phones. If every phone with this group is lost, a computer of the group or a new phone takes the group back with it, after the group\'s wait.
The sheet printed for the old key stops working.
The sheet printed for it stops working. Without a recovery key, losing every phone with this group loses the group.
The recovery key is removed. A sheet printed for it no longer works.
Print this sheet or save it as a PDF now. It shows only this once.
This phone forgets the key now. To get a sheet again, make a new recovery key.
QR code of the recovery key
Keep this sheet somewhere safe, away from your phones. Anyone who has it can take your group over, after the group\'s wait, unless the root phone cancels it.
To take the group back: on a new phone, choose Restore with a recovery key and scan the code; or on a computer of the group, run cbb recovery and type the key.
Put the recovery key on a YubiKey

The YubiKey makes the key in a free PIV slot, and the key never leaves it. Nothing else on the YubiKey changes. Restoring then needs the YubiKey, its PIN and a tap. A YubiKey with its own management key is not supported here: use the sheet instead.

Keep this phone on the network of a computer of the group. You hold the YubiKey to the phone twice: once to find the group, once to sign the claim. This phone becomes the group\'s root when the group\'s waiting time ends, unless the old phone cancels it.
Hold the YubiKey to the back of the phone until this message goes.
Found the group. Hold the YubiKey to the phone again to sign the claim.
The recovery key is on the YubiKey. Keep it away from this phone; a recovery sheet made before no longer works.
This card is not a YubiKey with PIV.
Wrong PIN. After three wrong tries the YubiKey blocks its PIN.
The YubiKey\'s PIN is blocked. Unblock it with its PUK in Yubico Authenticator, then try again.
This YubiKey is older than firmware 5.7, which the app needs to put a key on it. Print a recovery sheet instead.
This YubiKey has its own management key, which the app cannot use. Print a recovery sheet instead.
Every free PIV slot of this YubiKey is in use.
This YubiKey holds no recovery key of a group.
The YubiKey did not answer as expected. Hold it still against the phone and try again.
No YubiKey was held to the phone.
NFC is off. Turn it on in the phone\'s settings, then try again.
This phone has no NFC, which the YubiKey needs.

This phone\'s keys and the group\'s data here are deleted, and remote paste is turned off; the other settings stay. It can then join this group again or another one. The group keeps listing it until an admin removes it.
Deletes this phone\'s keys and the group\'s data here; the settings stay.
This phone holds the group\'s root: it leaves only once the group has no other devices.
This phone was removed from the group
The group\'s devices refuse it now. Leave the group to delete its keys here; then it can join a group again.
This phone is in no group, so there is nothing to leave.
This phone holds the group\'s root, and the group has other devices. Remove them first, or let an admin phone take the group over.
This phone takes no copies from the group for now.
This phone takes copies from the group again.
The device is muted: its copies stay its own.
An admin muted this phone, so its copies stay on it.
An admin muted this phone until %1$s: its copies stay on it.
An admin muted this phone: its copies stay on it until an admin unmutes it.
Not taking copies from the group
take no copies from the group
take copies from the group again
Muted until an admin unmutes it
Its copies then reach no device of the group; it still takes theirs.
